rows.description: I was caught cheating and my face is hot. I want to run away. A wise adult helps me say sorry and try again fairly. If I am called a bad child I may cheat better or stop playing.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: deceit, fairness, rivalry
related mind states: shame

rows.description: My older sibling makes up rules that always let him win. I feel angry and powerless. Wise: say "that is not fair" and ask a parent to help. Older siblings should learn that letting the small one win sometimes is kindness.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: deceit, rivalry, shame
related mind states: anger

rows.description: I open the box and it is socks, not a toy. My face drops. Wise: say thank you first and cry later at home if needed. Parents can teach that the gift is someone's love even if it is not what I wanted.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: gratitude, honesty, hurt
related mind states: affection, gratitude, sadness, disappointment

rows.description: I say "I don't like this" out loud in front of the giver. I am not being rude on purpose, I say what I feel. A wise parent shows a kind way: "thank you, it was kind of you", and later hears my real feeling.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: disillusionment, gratitude, hurt
related mind states: gratitude

rows.description: The child made a face at my gift and I feel sad. As the giver I understand small children do not hide feelings. A wise adult does not scold; they may say it lightly and remind the child gratefulness matters.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: disillusionment, gratitude, honesty
related mind states: gratitude, sadness, hurt

rows.description: I draw a card for my friend's birthday and give it with a big smile. I feel excited that they will like it. Giving something I made myself teaches that love is in the effort, not the price.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: gratitude, pride
this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12
related mind states: affection, excitement

rows.description: My friend gives me a drawing and I say "thank you, I love it" and hug it. I feel loved and want to give back. Saying thanks kindly teaches me how gifts make friendships warm.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: affection, pride
this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12
related mind states: affection, gratitude

rows.description: I give Papa a card I made and he puts it on the fridge. I feel proud. A parent who treasures a child's small gift teaches that giving is valued, and that my own effort matters.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: affection, gratitude
this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12
related mind states: pride

rows.description: I have a fever and Mummy holds me and sits by my bed. I feel small, warm and safe. Being cared for while sick teaches that I can be weak and still loved, and that resting is okay.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: dependence, envy, fear, trust
related mind states: affection, trust, empathy

rows.description: I am scared of the doctor's needle and cry. My heart thumps. A wise adult tells me the truth: "it will pinch for a second and I am here". Lying that it will not hurt makes the next visit harder.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: compassion, dependence, envy, trust
related mind states: sadness, fear, hurt
